column1: # The kernel-fix ledger: one row per kernel defect OCCTSwift has fixed, carried a fix for, or guards.
# WHY THIS EXISTS. A guard written for a kernel defect used to be retired from memory, and three of
# them outlived their fix because no test could say so (okf/references/known-occt-bugs.md). With two
# kernel flavours (hardened, which carries these patches, and LTS, which is vanilla OCCT) the same
# question has two answers, so it is written down once, here, and read by machines:
#   Scripts/emit-kernel-fixes-header.py  turns it into OCCTKernelFixes.h inside each kernel asset
#   Scripts/check-kernel-fixes.py        the gate: patches, rows, guards and tags must all agree
# COLUMNS (tab separated; lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored)
#   id           F + the four-digit patch number. Stable: never renumbered, never reused.
#   group        thread-safety | hardening | crash-guard | wrong-answer | ahead | absorbed
#                thread-safety, hardening and crash-guard change no result; wrong-answer and ahead
#                do, and are what the two flavours disagree about. absorbed: upstream took the fix.
#   defect       the patch's own name, which is what it fixes.
#   occt_ref     OCCT issues and pull requests for the same defect, whoever filed them, space
#                separated, or - when nothing is filed. A - on a carried row is the upstream worklist.
#   upstream_in  the first RELEASED OCCT version that holds the fix (8.0.2), or - when none does.
#                A patch whose file is retired and whose upstream_in is set stays here, as history.
#   relation     how upstream's fix relates to ours: identical | same-code | different-form |
# A FIX IS PRESENT in a kernel when upstream_in is at or below the OCCT version the kernel is built
# from, or, for the carry flavour only, when its patch file is in Scripts/patches. So the vanilla
# kernel holds exactly the rows upstream has absorbed, and the two shrink toward each other every time
# GUARDS AND TESTS name a row by tagging themselves `kernel-defect: F0080` and by testing the macro
# OCCTSWIFT_KERNEL_HAS_F0080 (or, in a test, the requiresKernelFix("F0080") trait). They are not
# listed here: the gate finds them, so there is no second list to drift.
# F0052 has no row: it was a doc comment (OCCT#1602, on IR and not in a release), changed no binary,
# and is not a defect a guard or a flavour could differ on.
